security_audit.summary: This skill contains legitimate setup scripts for creating and bundling React artifacts, but several confirmed risks remain because the scripts run shell commands, install public packages, modify project files, and extract an embedded archive. I did not find prompt-injection text or data-exfiltration intent in SKILL.md; most markdown backtick and hardcoded URL findings are false positives. The embedded archive appears to contain expected shadcn/ui source files after manual inspection.

remediation.suggestion: Pin all package versions, avoid npm install -g when possible, and include a lockfile or checksum guidance for reproducible installs.
Document every file and directory that scripts create, modify, or delete. Require explicit confirmation before running them in an agent workflow.
Accept only safe directory slugs, reject names starting with a dash, and reject absolute paths or parent-directory traversal.

remediation.issue: Embedded component archive reduces audit transparency
remediation.suggestion: Prefer plain source files in the skill repository, or publish a manifest and checksum that is verified before extraction.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Package Installation From Public Registries
semantic_findings.description: The scripts install pnpm globally, create a Vite project, and add many dependencies without pinned versions or integrity checks. This exposes users to supply-chain changes when the skill is run.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The package-install commands are explicit and several dependencies are unpinned or use latest. The risk is supply-chain exposure, not direct malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Project Directory Argument
semantic_findings.description: The initialization script uses the first argument as PROJECT_NAME, passes it to create-vite, then changes into that directory before writing configuration files. It should reject path traversal and option-like names.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The variable is quoted, which reduces shell injection risk, but no validation limits it to a safe local directory name. The subsequent writes make the argument safety relevant.

content.value_statement: Complex Claude artifacts need structured React projects, component libraries, and reliable bundling. This skill creates a Vite setup and packages it into a shareable single-file HTML artifact.
actual_capabilities: Creates a React 18 and TypeScript Vite project from a project name.
Adds Tailwind CSS 3.4.1 configuration with shadcn/ui theme variables.
Installs Radix UI and related shadcn/ui dependencies with pnpm.
Extracts bundled shadcn/ui components into the generated src directory.
Builds a Parcel bundle and inlines assets into bundle.html.
Documents optional local visualization with Playwright or Puppeteer.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer and pnpm availability.
Runs shell scripts that install packages and modify project files.
Designed for complex React artifacts, not simple static HTML snippets.
Bundled output still needs review for size, accessibility, and browser behavior.

prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate artifact with local state and reusable components.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a budget planning artifact with editable categories, totals, and validation. Use shadcn/ui components and bundle it as one HTML file.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced artifact with navigation and richer UI patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-view project status artifact with overview, timeline, and risks views. Use React state, Tailwind CSS, and accessible shadcn/ui components.

prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with build review and handoff notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a polished data exploration artifact, bundle it into bundle.html, and summarize dependency changes, assumptions, and manual review steps.

output_examples.output: A generated React project with Tailwind styling, shadcn/ui controls, and a bundled HTML file ready for review.

output_examples.input: Create a multi-panel dashboard for project health.
output_examples.output: A Vite-based artifact with reusable components, tabbed views, mock data, and a single-file HTML bundle.

output_examples.input: Package an interactive teaching demo for browser use.
output_examples.output: A self-contained artifact that combines React interaction, component styling, and inlined build assets.

best_practices: Run the initialization script only in a clean working directory.
Review package changes and bundled output before sharing the artifact.
Use this skill when the artifact needs reusable components or stateful views.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for a single static HTML page.
Do not run scripts inside a repository with unrelated unsaved work.
Do not skip dependency review when package versions are unpinned.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a React and TypeScript Vite project with Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui components, and a bundling workflow.

faq.question: Does it produce one shareable file?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundle script creates bundle.html with JavaScript, CSS, and assets inlined.

faq.question: Is this useful for simple HTML snippets?
faq.answer: No. It is intended for complex artifacts that need React components, state, or routing-like views.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does the skill install dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. Its scripts use pnpm and npm commands to install project, UI, and bundling dependencies.

faq.question: What should users review before running it?
faq.answer: Users should review the shell scripts, dependency commands, project directory name, and the generated bundle output.
